name: Congenital Intestinal Disease Due to an Enzymatic Defect

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient specific intestinal enzyme activity in biopsy or biochemical assay
Presence of chronic malabsorption symptoms from birth or early infancy
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes encoding the intestinal enzyme
Exclusion of other causes of congenital malabsorption such as structural abnormalities or infections

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic malabsorption symptoms plus demonstration of deficient intestinal enzyme activity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is supportive but not mandatory if enzyme deficiency is confirmed biochemically.

searchTerms: severe poor nutrient absorption from birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent osmotic diarrhea from neonatal period
Failure to thrive despite adequate feeding

searchTerms: imbalanced blood salts due to poor absorption
low blood minerals from gut issues

common.symptomName: Vitamin deficiencies (e.g., fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K)
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K

common.symptomName: Irritability and lethargy secondary to malnutrition

occasional.symptomName: Mild hepatomegaly due to metabolic stress

searchTerms: mild low red blood cells from poor absorption
low blood count due to malabsorption

occasional.symptomName: Mild hypotonia due to nutritional deficiencies

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to vitamin B12 deficiency
searchTerms: neurological symptoms due to vitamin B12 deficiency

rare.symptomName: Dermatological manifestations such as dermatitis from nutrient deficiencies
searchTerms: skin problems due to poor nutrition

rare.symptomName: Osteopenia or rickets secondary to vitamin D deficiency
searchTerms: bone thinning or rickets from vitamin D lack
weak bones due to vitamin D deficiency
osteopenia related to low vitamin D
immune deficiency due to poor nutrition

laboratory: Low or absent activity of specific intestinal enzymes in biopsy specimens
Steatorrhea with elevated fecal fat content
Vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K, B12) on serum testing
Anemia with microcytic or macrocytic features
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound may show mild hepatomegaly
Barium studies typically normal or nonspecific
Intestinal mucosal atrophy on endoscopic biopsy
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes encoding intestinal digestive enzymes (e.g., sucrase-isomaltase gene mutations)
other: Positive response to enzyme replacement therapy or dietary modification
Exclusion of infectious or structural causes of malabsorption

distinguishingFeatures: Specific enzyme deficiency limited to disaccharidase enzymes
Normal histology except for enzyme assay
Multi-system involvement including pulmonary and pancreatic insufficiency
Characteristic genetic mutations in CFTR gene
Histological villous atrophy reversible with gluten-free diet

redFlags: Severe failure to thrive despite nutritional support
Persistent severe osmotic diarrhea from birth
Electrolyte disturbances refractory to standard treatment
